subject: Opal.ai dedicated capacity: peaking curve, fallback allocation and proposal next steps
messages:
From: Ben Caldwell <ben.caldwell@opal.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask: peak shaping and latency SLOs

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking a look — we've been evaluating Redwood for a dedicated deployment and want to get concrete numbers for capacity planning. High level:

- Primary model: Open-Instruction-XL (approx 50B, 8k context) for our customer-facing chat.
- Typical request size: 1200 tokens input, ~800 tokens generated (avg).
- Expected steady-state: 400M tokens/day.
- Peaking pattern: a daily 3-hour window where traffic concentrates; observed peak TPS 10x baseline; estimated peak tokens/sec ~ 1,200 tokens/sec.
- SLO target: p95 generation latency <= 1.6s (we currently measure p95 ~1.2s on another provider).

Can you produce a short sizing sketch with: tokens/sec estimates, GPU node types recommended, a quantized variant fallback for cost control, and a practical headroom factor (we'll need justification for commits)? Attaching a short doc with our traff ic sample.

Also include anything we should expect on cold-start / KV cache warmup during the peaking window. Procurement copied for timeline visibility.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call after your initial note.

Best,
Ben Caldwell
Head of Platform
Opal.ai

Attachments: opal_requirements.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Caldwell <ben.caldwell@opal.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: peak shaping and latency SLOs

Ben — thanks for the detail. Quick reply with a first-pass operational sketch; we'll follow with a short spreadsheet and a proposed contract delta.

Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Model compute: Open-Instruction-XL -> peak decode cost in our profile: ~0.00095 GPU-seconds/token on A100-class kernels (non-quantized).
- Peak tokens/sec target: 1,200 tokens/sec (as you noted).
- Desired p95 <= 1.6s for the 2k token generation tail (we'll size for worst-case generation length).

Sizing summary (first pass):
- Baseline dedicated pool: 6x A100-80GB instances (pod-level serving with 8 GPUs total across nodes) gives sustained throughput ~480 tokens/sec for the model as-is (single replica serving with batching).
- Peak handling: add a 2x burst buffer (autoscaled reserved nodes) — target pool = 18 GPUs equivalent to hit ~1,200 tokens/sec with headroom. That maps to ~3 replicas sharded across 6 nodes (topology depends on your networking).
- Headroom & safety: recommend commit that covers 1.8x of observed peak (we recommend 2.0–2.5x for commercial commitments depending on seasonality). For Opal's pattern, 2.0x should be defensible.
- Cost-control options: 8-bit quantized variant (Q8) reduces inference cost ~1.8x at ~2–4% QoE regressions — good candidate for off-peak or burst fallback.
- Cold-start/KV: expect a 40–120s warmup for KV cache to reach steady hit rates for long context sessions; suggest a cross-warmup prefetch strategy (keep a small always-warm pool during the 3-hour peak).

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik and I will produce an "ops-grade" sizing spreadsheet with tokens/sec math, per-GPU throughput, and estimated monthly committed cost — target EOD tomorrow.
2) We'll include a fallback routing policy: primary = non-quantized model on dedicated pool; fallback = quantized variant (or lower context) once utilization > 85% for > 60s.
3) If procurement is comfortable, we'll draft a short delta to the MSA that covers burst overlay credit and canary rollout windows.

I'm attaching the initial sizing workbook. Karthik — can you add the per-replica decode math and a conservative p95 projection? Marissa, can you prepare a short bullet list for procurement that summarizes the commit / burst overlay options?

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Caldwell <ben.caldwell@opal.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: peak shaping and latency SLOs

Looping in more detail on the throughput math and SLO fit. Mina's high-level looks correct; adding numbers you can cite to procurement.

Throughput math (conservative):
- Measured decode cost: 0.00095 GPU-sec/token (A100-80GB) -> 1 GPU can decode ~1,050 tokens/sec sustained with our batching profile for this model.
- Steady baseline 400M tokens/day -> ~4,630 tokens/sec avg across 24h; however your reported daily distribution indicates heavy concentration. (Note: your average implies higher than your quoted peak, so I'm assuming your 400M/day is the monthly average; please confirm.)
- For peak 1,200 tokens/sec target: approx 2 GPUs sustained (1,050 tokens/sec per gpu), but to hit p95 <= 1.6s under real-world concurrent session patterns we need replication + batching headroom.

Recommended deployment topology (conservative sizing):
- Dedicated pool: 8 GPUs (A100-80GB) spread across 4 nodes (2 GPUs/node) — handles steady baseline with spare capacity for concurrency.
- Burst overlay: +12 GPUs (4 nodes of 3 GPUs) dedicated as autoscaling overlay; all-in peak capacity 20 GPUs -> theoretical decode ~21,000 tokens/sec (but real-world delivered ~14–16k tokens/sec after accounting for queueing and KV overhead). We do not expect to need all of that, but it gives a safety buffer for multi-tenanted noise and can be dialed down to 10–12 GPUs in practice.

SLO fit and headroom reasoning:
- p95 latency drivers: batching latency, KV cache miss penalty, and scheduling jitter. To keep p95 <= 1.6s we budget ~0.9s for decode, ~0.4s for batching/scheduling, ~0.3s for KV misses. The sizing above keeps decode under budget with a 1.8x headroom on sustained throughput.
- Fallback model variants: Q8 quantized variant reduces GPU-sec/token to ~0.00055; effective throughput uplift ~1.7x. Route 15% of requests to quantized during peak transients to smooth tails, full fallback if utilization > 92% for 90s.

Operational notes:
- Canary & rollout: 10% traffic to dedicated pool for first 24h, increase with observed p95 stability.
- Cost engineering: if Opal wants tighter committed spend, we can offer a burst-credit pool (monthly usage credits for burst GPU-hours) rather than hard commit for additional nodes.

I'll add the per-GPU numbers to Mina's spreadsheet and produce a short chart showing the peaking curve vs. capacity plan.

-Karthik
Principal Infra SE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina, Karthik — this is exactly the level we needed. A few quick items from procurement and product: 

- Procurement would like a formal proposal that lists: committed GPUs, burst overlay credit option, estimated monthly committed cost, and a short fallback SLA (what we get if you route to quantized model).
- Product asked for expected cold-start behavior during the peak window; the cross-warmup approach makes sense—can you include an expected hit-rate warmup curve?
- Timeline: we're aiming to be live in early August. Procurement attached our timeline.

If you can send a one-page proposal and the updated sizing sheet by EOD July 6, we'll aim to review and schedule a contract call the following week. Also — please include a short blurb on rollback criteria for canary (we need clear ops exit conditions).

I'll hold a 30m slot next Thursday for the proposal review; I'll send a calendar invite once we receive your doc.

Best,
Ben
